html:
A mountain country of Central Asia in the Tian Shan and Pamir ranges, independent since August 1991. The map shows it in 1994 and 2010.

The Kyrgyz were nomadic herders, and their oral Epic of Manas is among the longest poems in the world. Russia conquered the land in the 19th century; a revolt in 1916 was crushed, and many Kyrgyz made the flight to China.

After the Soviet Union dissolved, Askar Akayev made Kyrgyzstan at first the most open state in the region. It also proved the least stable. The Tulip Revolution drove Akayev out in 2005, and a second uprising toppled his successor Kurmanbek Bakiyev in 2010. That summer, violence between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks around Osh in the south killed hundreds and drove many from their homes, in the 2010 clashes. A new constitution then made the country a parliamentary republic, rare in Central Asia, though strong presidential rule returned in 2021. The capital is Bishkek.
